config.brief:
Research the COMPANY in the base profile (traits.company; the person's title is only context) to learn how it builds and activates customer audiences today. Use public business sources only: the company's own site and engineering or data blog, its current job postings (lifecycle, CRM, marketing operations, analytics and data engineering roles usually name the warehouse and marketing tools the team uses: fetch one or two and read the requirements), vendor case studies and customer pages that name the company, press, and conference talks by its staff. Never research the individual person, their personal life, contact details or anyone's private data.

Find, in this order:
1. What the company sells and to whom, in one plain sentence.
2. Its cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift or similar), only when a source names it for this company.
3. The marketing and activation tools it uses to reach customers (for example Braze, Iterable, Customer.io, Klaviyo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Segment, mParticle, Hightouch, Census, RudderStack, Google Ads, Meta Ads), only when a source names them for this company.
4. How audiences get built today, when a source says it: for example lifecycle marketers writing SQL, a data team fielding segment requests, a reverse-ETL sync, or a CDP.
5. One public item from the last six months (<MONTH YEAR> or later) that a lifecycle or data leader there would care about: a product or programme launch, a loyalty or personalisation change, a data or CRM case study, a talk by their staff, or open lifecycle, CRM or data roles. Brand campaigns, celebrity or spokesperson news and general marketing news do not qualify. Nothing older qualifies; leave it empty rather than use an older item, and never use a menu, a price list or a routine product page.

Rules: report only what a source states about THIS company; a tool listed on its own job post counts, a generic industry claim does not. When unsure, leave the field empty rather than guess, and never fill a field with a sentence saying nothing was found: an empty field already says that. Prefer one strong source over several weak ones. Write facts plainly, no marketing language.

outputs.label: What they sell
outputs.description: One plain sentence: what the company sells and to whom. Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Cloud warehouse
outputs.description: The warehouse a source names for this company (e.g. Snowflake). Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Marketing and activation tools
outputs.description: Marketing, CRM and activation tools a source names for this company. Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: How audiences are built today
outputs.description: What a source says about how the company builds and syncs audiences today (who builds segments, with what). Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Recent company item
outputs.description: One public item from the last six months that a lifecycle or data leader would care about, stated neutrally with its month. Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Main source
outputs.description: The URL of the strongest source behind these fields.

config.brief:
Find what this person publicly works on and talks about in their professional role. The base profile gives their name, title and company in traits; their LinkedIn handle is the part of userId after 'linkedin:' (linkedin:janedoe means linkedin.com/in/janedoe).

Search, in this order, and stop once you have one solid item:
1. Their LinkedIn posts and articles: search `site:linkedin.com/posts/<handle>` and `site:linkedin.com/pulse "<full name>" <company>`.
2. Talks, podcasts, webinars and interviews: search `"<full name>" <company> podcast`, `"<full name>" <company> webinar OR talk OR panel`, `"<full name>" <company> interview`.
3. Anything they wrote on the company blog or a trade publication.
Topics that matter most: lifecycle and CRM marketing, retention, loyalty, personalisation, segmentation and audience building, growth, marketing data and working with data teams.

Identity: an item counts only when it clearly belongs to this person (same full name AND their current or a past company, or the same LinkedIn handle). Two people can share a name; when you cannot tell, use nothing.

Never collect anything about their personal life, family, location, health, politics, contact details or anything that is not their public work. Do not infer opinions they have not stated. An item older than two years is fine for focus but say its year. When nothing qualifies, leave every field empty: an empty answer is a correct answer.

outputs.label: Public work focus
outputs.description: One sentence on what this person publicly talks about or works on in their role, from their own posts, talks or articles. Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Recent public item
outputs.description: One specific item of theirs (post, talk, article, podcast): what it was about and its month and year. Leave it empty when no source says so; never write a sentence saying nothing was found.

outputs.label: Source
outputs.description: The URL of the item the fields rest on.
